shared_blind_spot.name: shared_blind_spot

predictions.depends_on: The 50 percent contamination cells for reader Q with writers Q-self, E-self and G-self at 4 seeds, harm defined as S(clean) - S(contaminated) against the shared clean base cell, contaminant lengths matched across writers by selection.
predictions.falsifier: Foreign-writer failures harm as much or more than the reader's own, or all writers fall below Gate 0.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Harm is already a cell difference, so harm(Q-self) - harm(foreign) is a difference of differences whose paired CI is roughly sqrt(2) times the stated +/-8 net floor (about +/-8 even at 4 seeds), while the margin is 4 net - inside the noise; the criterion is also disjunctive (Q-self must beat E-self or G-self by 4), which lets the prediction pass on the smaller of two comparisons and makes the stated falsifier strictly harder to reach than a pre-registered single contrast would be.
predictions.fix: Pre-register one named foreign comparator (or require Q-self to exceed the maximum of E-self and G-self), state the paired MDE for the double difference, and set the margin above it - or raise seeds/rates until the double-difference CI half-width is below 3 net.

predictions.depends_on: The 50 percent cells for Q-self, Q-prox and E-self as writers for reader Q; Q-prox's construction and its pi manipulation check are inherited from the matrix design and are not specified in this proposal.
predictions.falsifier: Q-prox equals Q-self within 1 net while E-self differs, or the harm order is non-monotone.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The ordering is asserted with 2-net gaps on each side of Q-prox and a 1-net equivalence in the falsifier, on double differences whose stated noise floor is +/-8 net (about +/-8 even after the 4-seed upgrade), so both the predicted monotone gradient and its falsifier are pure noise draws; a non-monotone order will in fact occur by chance a large fraction of the time regardless of the hypothesis, and the proximity manipulation itself (pi lower by >= 0.15 at matched k=0) is not defined or checked inside this proposal.
predictions.fix: Restate the gradient as a slope over a measured pi axis with more than three writers and a pre-registered CI, restate Q-prox's construction and manipulation check here, and set the margins from a stated double-difference MDE rather than at 1-2 net.

predictions.depends_on: The offline judge x writer recall table on 400 masked items per writer (4 writers x 2-3 judges) at matched precision, with memory-absent abstention checks and the judges' overall recall as a covariate; the test is the judge x writer interaction, not a main effect.
predictions.falsifier: Recall is uniform across writers for each judge, or one judge is uniformly better with no diagonal deficit.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Both outcomes are mechanically reachable - detectability could be a property of the item text alone, which the design allows to show up as a writer main effect - and the power is adequate for once: Wilson SE is about 0.025 at n = 400, so a recall difference of two cells has SE about 0.035 and the 0.15 threshold sits at roughly 4 SE, with the interaction framing and the memory-absent abstention check blocking the uniformly-better-judge and always-no artifacts.

predictions.depends_on: The unmasked detection cells, where items keep the terminal failure line, scored on the same judge x writer table.
predictions.falsifier: The diagonal deficit persists at >= 0.05 with the failure line visible, or some cell's recall falls below 0.85.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The unmasked arm restores the explicit terminal failure line - the exact token the detection judgment is scored on - so recall is at ceiling for any judge that reads the item, and a ceiling compresses every cell difference toward zero; the falsifier is reachable only through a mechanism the proposal never names or controls (a judge that reads an explicit failure line and still calls the item a success), and the 0.05 band is itself only about 1.5 SE of a paired recall difference at n = 400.
predictions.fix: Add a graded-evidence arm between masked and unmasked (failure line removed but the failed terminal state or the unrecovered subgoal left intact) so the deficit has room to persist off ceiling, and state the deficit-shrinkage test as an interaction CI rather than a sub-0.05 point band.

predictions.depends_on: The two filter cells at 25 percent Q-self contamination (own-judgment filter, cross-judge filter) at 2 seeds, with recovery expressed as a fraction of the harm at that rate.
predictions.falsifier: The own filter recovers within 15 percentage points of the cross filter, or neither recovers 30 percent of the harm.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The denominator is the harm at 25 percent, roughly half the Gate-0 effect defined at 50 percent (6 net), so 60 percent recovery is about 1.8 net points and the 30 percent boundary about 0.9 net, all measured in cells at 2 seeds against a stated +/-8 net floor - the entire predicted-versus-falsifying interval is an order of magnitude inside the noise; the ordering is also largely inherited from P3, since filter recovery at matched precision is a monotone function of the same recall gap.
predictions.fix: Run the filter arms at the 50 percent rate where the harm is >= 6 net, at 4+ seeds, and state the criterion in net points recovered with a paired CI - or evaluate the filters offline on removed-contaminant counts, where n = 400 per writer gives real power.

predictions.depends_on: The graft cells at 25 and 50 percent (expert items with procedure-specific steps swapped) and the length-matched clean placebo at 50 percent, 2 seeds.
predictions.falsifier: The graft costs < 6 net at 50 percent, or the length-matched clean placebo costs >= 6 net.
predictions.label: entailed
predictions.reason: The proposal itself removes the first falsifier from play - a graft below 6 net is declared a design failure to be redone with a harsher graft, so the protocol iterates the positive control until it passes and the outcome can never stand against the hypothesis - while the placebo half is an equivalence claim (<= 3 net) whose falsifying value (6) is inside the stated +/-8 2-seed floor, so it cannot resolve either.
predictions.fix: Pre-register a fixed graft recipe with at most one named re-specification, report the failed version, and treat a persistent sub-6 graft as the reported negative it is; give the placebo 4+ seeds and an upper-CI-bound criterion instead of a point margin under the noise floor.

shared_terms: P1-P2: harm(Q-self) and harm(E-self) at 50 percent are literally the same two cell differences in both predictions, so P2's >= 4 net Q-self-minus-E-self requirement is P1's comparison re-used and one determines the other.

P3-P4: the same judge x writer table and the same 400-item sets, with P4 scoring the paired unmasked version of the identical items, so the two deficits share the per-writer item sample and the matched-precision thresholds.
P3-P5: filter recovery at matched precision is a monotone function of the P3 recall gap on the same masked items, so a confirmed P3 largely fixes P5's ordering before any episode is run.
P1-P6: harm and graft cost both subtract the same clean base cell (rate 0), so an error in that single cell moves every harm estimate, the graft's Gate-0 check and the placebo bound together.
P1-P5: the 25 percent recovery denominator is the harm slope fitted through the same 50 percent Q-self cell that P1 tests, so P1's estimate scales P5's percentages.
shared_blind_spot.headline: P1

coverage_not_headcount.name: coverage_not_headcount

predictions.depends_on: HET-cap N=4 store {Qwen3-32B ReAct, EXAONE, gpt-oss-120b, expert item-matched} at B/4 each vs self(B) at k=3 and vs the Measurement-C static-procedure prompt, Qwen3-32B reader, paired on 274 games x 4 seeds (paired CI ~+/-4.5), with per-type s_w(t) profiles from collection logs.
predictions.falsifier: Gain over self(B) <= +4 net, or <= 50% of that gain falling in types where some writer's s_w(t) >= s_R(t)+0.2, or HET-cap <= static-procedure + 4.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: The static-procedure branch is genuinely reachable (nothing in the design forces retrieval to beat a per-type static prompt by more than 4 net), even though the vs-self(B) branch is pre-loaded by HET-cap containing the expert quarter whose Measurement-A gain on heat/clean/cool is +39..+55 while self(B) has no expert items, and the localization branch is close to forced by headroom (gain can only appear where the reader fails, which is where max_w s_w(t) - s_R(t) is large).

predictions.depends_on: Spearman rho between gain-over-own-matched-pool and the frozen coverage complement C across >= 12 store x reader cells, plus partial correlations of N and diversity class with C controlled; cell gains carry +/-4.5 (4 seeds) to +/-8 (2 seeds).
predictions.falsifier: rho < 0.4, or N or diversity class showing partial |rho| >= 0.5, or a >= 6 net difference between the equal-coverage N=4 control and the N=2 store of identical C.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: With n = 12 cells and each cell's gain carrying +/-4.5 to +/-8 net, the sampling CI on a Spearman rho spans roughly 0.2-0.9 and no CI or MDE for rho or for the partial correlations is stated anywhere in Measurement and Noise Control, so the 0.4 / 0.7 boundary and the 0.3 / 0.5 partial boundary are decided by noise rather than by data.
predictions.fix: Pre-register a bootstrap CI for rho and the partials (resampling games jointly with cells) and either expand to ~30+ store x reader cells or promote the equal-coverage N=4 vs N=2 paired contrast to the primary, powered test of the headline claim.

predictions.depends_on: self(B/2) + dominated-writer(B/2) vs self(B) at k=3, dominated writer selected from measured profiles (else Qwen3-32B at T=1.2 collected), 4 seeds, paired differences about +/-4.5.
predictions.falsifier: Gain change <= -6 net (item count governs) or >= +6 net (phrasing diversity governs).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: This is an equivalence claim whose asserted band [-4, +4] is narrower than the stated +/-4.5 paired CI, so no run at the planned power can affirm it and the [4, 6] and [-6, -4] decision gaps sit entirely inside the noise; no TOST or equivalence-power calculation is given.
predictions.fix: Run the dominated-displacement cell at enough seeds for a paired CI of about +/-2 (or widen the equivalence band past the noise to +/-6 with falsification at +/-9) and pre-register a two-one-sided-test rule.

predictions.depends_on: Ratio of HET-cap's gain over self(B) on heat/clean/cool to the expert-only bank's gain over self(B) on those types at matched item count, per type, Qwen3-32B reader.
predictions.falsifier: The ratio is <= 40% with CI excluding 60%.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The expert walkthrough writer is itself one of HET-cap's four writers, so the numerator contains the denominator's items and the claimed reading ('model writers recover most of what the expert writer gives') is not tested by any arm; the falsifier is reachable only through crowding-out of expert items in the top-3, a mechanism the proposal neither names nor controls, and the arm that would show the opposite (a model-writers-only store) is absent.
predictions.fix: Add a model-writers-only store (Qwen3-32B ReAct + EXAONE + gpt-oss-120b at B/3 each, item-matched to the expert bank) as P4's numerator, keeping HET-cap as a secondary cell.

predictions.depends_on: Conflict rate (fraction of top-3 sets with >= 2 distinct parsed skeletons for the type) logged over the N in {1,2,4,8} grid, plus its partial correlation with gain once C is controlled, on the same >= 12 cells as P2.
predictions.falsifier: Conflict rate showing partial rho <= -0.5 with gain once C is controlled.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The falsifier is a partial correlation over the same tiny cell grid with no stated CI or MDE, and conflict rate is nearly collinear with N and with store composition, so -0.5 cannot be separated from -0.3 or 0; the first clause (conflict rises 0.15 from N=2 to N=8) carries no falsifier at all and is essentially a counting consequence of splitting a fixed budget across more writers of different scaffolds and backbones.
predictions.fix: State a bootstrap CI for the partial rho, and decorrelate conflict from N with a skeleton-matched N=8 store (same-skeleton writers) versus a skeleton-varied N=8 store at equal C so conflict is manipulated rather than merely observed.

shared_terms: P1-P4: HET-cap's gain over self(B) on heat/clean/cool is P1's headline magnitude and P4's ratio numerator, so a large P1 result mechanically satisfies P4.
P1-P2: the HET-cap and self(B) cells are both grid points feeding the P2 correlation, so P1's outcome moves rho directly.

P2-P5: both are partial correlations with C controlled over the identical >= 12-cell set, and N, diversity class and conflict rate are functions of the same store composition, so one partial determines the others.
P3-P2: the dominated-displacement cell is the near-zero-C anchor of P2's correlation, so a P3 null is also what makes rho large.
coverage_not_headcount.headline: P2

one_bad_apple_population_vote.name: one_bad_apple_population_vote

predictions.depends_on: Procedure grafts (procedure step swapped or deleted) at controlled retrieved share 1, all top-3 items poisoned, on heat/clean/cool, Qwen3-32B reader at k=3, clean store P as the paired reference, 4 seeds, paired differences about +/-6.
predictions.falsifier: Harm < 6 net with CI excluding 6 (the reader takes procedures from its prior rather than from the retrieved item).
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The proposal's own Measurement-A figure of +39..+55 net memory gain on exactly these types means the reader is already known to take procedures from retrieved items, so replacing all three retrieved items with wrong procedures can miss 6 net only if the reader is near-insensitive to top-3 content (a mechanism that would contradict the cited gain and is not modelled); the falsification rule compounds this by demanding a CI excluding 6 when the stated half-width is itself 6, so only a measured harm of about zero could ever falsify.
predictions.fix: State the Gate-0 prediction as a fraction of the clean-store gain on the same types (e.g. grafts destroy >= 50% of the +39..+55 gain) with a symmetric CI rule, so the outcome is not forced by the size of the already-measured memory effect.

predictions.depends_on: Ratio of paired harm at controlled share 1/3 to paired harm at share 1 for grafts, k=3, positions randomized, 4 seeds, each harm carrying about +/-6.
predictions.falsifier: Harm at share 1/3 is <= 40% of harm at share 1 (harm proportional to share).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The 40%/60% boundary is 20% of a share-1 harm that Gate 0 only guarantees to be >= 6 net, so the decision band can be as small as about 1.2 net against two paired estimates each at +/-6, and no minimum share-1 harm or ratio CI half-width is pre-registered.
predictions.fix: Pre-register a minimum share-1 harm (e.g. >= 20 net) before the ratio test is run, plus a seed count giving a joint-bootstrap ratio CI of about +/-0.15.

predictions.depends_on: Natural planting at fixed n_p (expected share about 0.1 per target type), k in {1,3,7} on the poisoned store against the clean store at the same k, paired.
predictions.falsifier: Harm at k=7 <= harm at k=3 + 3 net (harm follows expected share, which is constant in k).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: At an expected share of about 0.1 the harm at k=3 will itself be a small fraction of the Gate-0 harm (plausibly 1-4 net), so the '2x' and '+3 net' boundaries and the k=1 'half' clause all lie well inside the stated +/-6 paired noise, and the k arms are additionally confounded because the clean-store reference changes with k.
predictions.fix: Raise n_p (or restrict to types) until harm at k=3 is at least the +/-6 noise, and pre-register the CI on the k=7 minus k=3 harm difference rather than on each harm separately.

predictions.depends_on: Dilution cells with fixed n_p and benign writers covering the target type increased 1 -> 2 -> 4 under natural retrieval (expected share falling about 0.5 -> 0.2), with recovery expressed as a fraction of the Gate-0 (share-1) harm at k=3.
predictions.falsifier: >= 50% of the Gate-0 harm is recovered by going from 1 to 4 benign writers.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: Recovery is scored against a denominator (share-1 harm, all top-3 poisoned) strictly larger than the harm actually present in the 1-writer dilution cell at share ~0.5, so the recoverable quantity is capped below the 50% threshold whenever that cell's harm is under half the Gate-0 harm, and nothing in the design guarantees it is not.
predictions.fix: Express recovery as a fraction of the harm measured in the 1-writer dilution cell (the quantity that can actually be recovered), and report the 1-writer cell's harm against Gate-0 harm separately.

predictions.depends_on: Relabelled failures (own failed train trajectories labelled success) vs procedure grafts, both at share 1 on target types, Qwen3 reader, with an escape clause routing the arm out if relabelled failures fail Gate 0.
predictions.falsifier: Relabelled harm >= graft harm - 2 net.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The gap between the predicted region (relabelled <= half of graft harm) and the falsifier (relabelled >= graft harm - 2) is only about half the graft harm minus 2, i.e. roughly 4 net if graft harm is at the Gate-0 floor of 6-12, while the difference of two paired harms each at +/-6 carries about +/-8.
predictions.fix: Condition the comparison on a graft harm large enough (e.g. >= 20 net) that the half-versus-minus-2 gap exceeds the difference CI, and report the relabelled-minus-graft difference with its own bootstrap CI.

predictions.depends_on: D1 cross-writer skeleton vote at m=8 with >= 3 independent benign writers in the vote pool versus D1-self (same m, own-writer pool only), scored on planted graft labels over thousands of retrieved items with Wilson CIs, parser validated on 100 hand-labelled items.
predictions.falsifier: D1-self within 0.1 of D1 (one writer's redundancy suffices), or D1 recall < 0.5.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Both falsifying outcomes are genuinely reachable - grafts are made by editing one of a writer's own successful trajectories, so that writer's remaining same-type items form a competent self-vote pool, and parser or natural-skeleton-variation failure can hold D1 recall under 0.5 - and Wilson CIs over thousands of retrieved items resolve 0.1-0.2 recall differences comfortably.

predictions.depends_on: D1 versus D3 versus no detector at share 2/3, with recovery scored as a fraction of the Gate-0 harm and cost as per-episode token overhead (D1 uses the programmatic ALFWorld parser, D3 spends ~500 LLM tokens per retrieved item).
predictions.falsifier: D1 recovers < 50% of the harm, or D3 recovers more than D1 at equal token overhead.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The token clause is true by construction (a programmatic parser cannot exceed 10% of a 500-token-per-item LLM critique) and the 'at equal token overhead' branch names a condition the two detectors can never occupy, leaving only the recovery threshold, whose 50%/70% band is about 20% of a share-2/3 harm plausibly in the 10-20 net range and therefore inside the stated +/-6 paired noise.
predictions.fix: Drop the token clause from the falsifier (report cost descriptively), state whether the denominator is the share-2/3 harm or the share-1 Gate-0 harm, and pre-register the seeds needed for a recovery-ratio CI of about +/-0.15.

predictions.depends_on: Carrier writer (Qwen3-written vs EXAONE-written grafts with identical wrong procedure content) crossed with reader (Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B) at share 2/3; the EXAONE cells are not in the listed 4-seed set (Gate-0, share-1/3, k-sweep), so they run at 2 seeds.
predictions.falsifier: The foreign carrier harms as much or more for either reader (harm depends on content only).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The falsifier is stated with no margin at all ('as much or more'), so with paired harm differences at about +/-6 (wider still for the 2-seed EXAONE arm) a true null falsifies or confirms roughly at chance and the interaction cannot be read off the data.
predictions.fix: State a margin for the carrier effect (e.g. own-carrier harm exceeds foreign-carrier harm by >= 6 net for each reader) and run all four carrier x reader cells at 4 seeds.

shared_terms: P1-P2: the share-1 graft harm is P1's estimand and P2's denominator, so a Gate 0 that barely passes shrinks P2's 40/60 band below the stated noise.
P1-P4: the same share-1 Gate-0 harm is P4's recovery denominator, which is what caps P4's falsifier.
P1-P7: the Gate-0 harm is again the denominator of D1's recovery fraction, so P1's magnitude sets whether P7 is resolvable.
P1-P5: graft harm at share 1 is both P1's estimand and P5's comparison term.
P2-P3: both are ratios of harms measured against the same clean-store reference at k=3, so the k=3 harm term appears in both.
P6-P7: D1's recall and precision on grafts determine the filtering recovery scored in P7, so P7 cannot come out well if P6 comes out badly.
one_bad_apple_population_vote.headline: P2

who_gets_read.name: who_gets_read

predictions.depends_on: Offline retrieval-share audit on store M (equal per-type item counts from four writers, so a 0.25 store share) with Q-task vs Q-traj queries built from existing k=0 logs, raw vs canonical item formats, dense full-text and BM25 indexes, Qwen3 and EXAONE readers, over 274 games x 2 seeds with per-type bootstrap.
predictions.falsifier: Q-traj excess on canonical items < 0.03 (homophily is formatting only), or Q-traj raw excess < 0.05 (no homophily), or Q-task excess >= 0.15 (a document-style prior drives it).
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: The canonical clause is the load-bearing one and is genuinely reachable, since canonical items are actions and observations from ALFWorld's fixed programmatic action vocabulary and environment-generated text, giving all four writers near-identical surface form; the audit is deterministic over thousands of retrievals, so its standard errors (about 0.01-0.03) separate the 0.03 and 0.08 thresholds.

predictions.depends_on: M-uniform under Q-traj@3 vs Q-task@3 with injection held at step 3 so only the query differs, Qwen3-32B reader at k=3, on types where a foreign writer's s_w(t) exceeds self's by >= 0.2, paired, 4 seeds (paired differences about +/-4.5), with Q-task@0 as the timing control.
predictions.falsifier: The difference is within +/-4 net, or Q-traj is better.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: The falsifying region contains the null and the a priori likely outcome (a richer query can just as easily improve retrieval relevance), the injection-timing confound is controlled by holding both arms at step 3, and type selection uses collection-log s_w(t) rather than any term shared with the outcome; only the 4-to-6 net decision gap sits inside the +/-4.5 CI.

predictions.depends_on: Uniform / proximity / global / per-type writer-side re-rankers over the same retriever scores on M under Q-task@0, alpha frozen on a 60-game train slice, same reader, 4 seeds, complementary types defined by collection-log s_w(t).
predictions.falsifier: Proximity weighting >= quality weighting - 2 net (proximity governs), or quality weighting <= uniform + 4 net (the retriever's implicit weighting already matches the writer's record).
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Nothing in the design forces a re-ranker that only reorders which of k=3 items come from which writer within a fixed store to beat uniform by more than 4 net, the random re-ranking placebo at matched alpha controls the act of re-ranking itself, and both falsifying branches are ordinary outcomes rather than excluded ones.

predictions.depends_on: Reader-side calibrated weights fitted on c=20 train games per writer x type (480 episodes per reader) vs writer-side s_w(t) weights, plus the ratio of Qwen3-calibrated weights used by EXAONE to EXAONE's own calibrated gain over uniform.
predictions.falsifier: Calibration adds >= 6 net over writer-side weights, or the mismatched weights retain < 40% of the matched gain.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: A per-cell success rate estimated from 20 episodes carries a standard error of about 0.11, so the calibrated weights are dominated by sampling noise and will add little regardless of whether reader-specific compatibility exists - the falsifier is reachable only through an estimator-quality mechanism the proposal never models - and the transfer clause compounds this because its denominator (EXAONE's own calibration gain over uniform) is the very quantity the first clause predicts to be near zero, making the >= 70% ratio undefined exactly when the prediction holds.
predictions.fix: Raise c (e.g. 100 games per writer x type), report the calibration weights' sampling error, add an oracle reader-side weighting fitted on validation outcomes as the ceiling arm, and pre-register a minimum matched-calibration gain below which the retention ratio is not computed.

predictions.depends_on: Retained-gain ratio of M-uniform and M-per-type to the best of four single-writer stores (self, prox, cap, expert) at equal per-type item count, joint bootstrap over games, cells at about +/-5.7 net.
predictions.falsifier: Uniform M >= best single-writer store (mixing is free), or the re-ranked ratio < 0.9.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The denominator is the maximum of four noisy single-writer gains, each cell carrying about +/-5.7 net, so the winner's curse inflates it by several net points and biases the <= 0.9 clause toward true independently of any real mixing cost; separately, a 0.1 change in the ratio is only about 2 net on plausible gain sizes and sits inside the stated paired noise.
predictions.fix: Pre-specify the comparator single-writer store (or select the best writer on a held-out train slice and score it on validation) so the denominator is not a post hoc maximum, and state the ratio CI half-width the seed plan delivers.

shared_terms: P1-P2: the Q-traj self-share excess audited in P1 is the mechanism whose downstream cost P2 scores, and both are computed from the same Q-traj retrievals, so a null in P1 leaves P2 with nothing to attribute the contrast to.
P3-P5: the M-per-type quality re-ranking gain over uniform is P3's headline quantity and P5's ratio numerator, so given the fixed single-writer denominators one determines the other.
P3-P4: writer-side per-type weighting's gain is the treatment in P3 and the baseline that P4's calibrated weights must beat by < 4 net.
P4 internal: EXAONE's own calibrated gain over uniform is both the quantity predicted to be small and the denominator of the >= 70% transfer ratio.
P5-P3: the best-single-writer gain is P5's denominator and the implicit ceiling on P3's re-ranking gain over uniform.
who_gets_read.headline: P3

compression_erases_the_writer.name: compression_erases_the_writer

predictions.depends_on: Self cells Q->Qwen3 and X->EXAONE, L0 vs L2 at matched injected tokens, paired by game and seed over 674 games x 2 seeds; stated per-cell half-width ~+-5 net, so a two-cell contrast is ~+-6.
predictions.falsifier: The 95% CI of D(self) lies entirely below +4 in either self cell (the writer's own procedures are at least as good as its raw trajectories).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The +4 margin sits inside the design's own noise (two-cell contrast half-width ~+-6, and the pre-registered seed escalation only triggers above +-6), so the natural anti-hypothesis outcome D(self)~0 gives a CI straddling +4 and falsifies nothing.
predictions.fix: Restate the falsifier as 'CI excludes +4 from below' so a null falsifies, and pre-register 4+ seeds on both self L0/L2 cells until the contrast half-width is <= 2.

predictions.depends_on: Foreign cells X->Qwen3 and Q->EXAONE, L0 vs L1 and L0 vs L2, token-matched, same fixed retriever and same paired games; L1 cells are outside the four headline cells the escalation amendment covers.
predictions.falsifier: CI of D(foreign) entirely above -4 in BOTH foreign cells (raw foreign at least as good as compressed foreign).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: -4 is inside the ~+-6 contrast noise and the falsifier is conjunctive over both foreign cells, so a flat D(foreign)~0, or one cell in which raw foreign wins, refutes nothing.
predictions.fix: Make falsification per-cell with a CI that must exclude 0 in the predicted direction, and extend the seed escalation to the L1 cells so every contrast has half-width <= 2.

predictions.depends_on: The four cells self-L0, self-L2, foreign-L0, foreign-L2 for each reader; interaction half-width ~+-8, ~+-6 after the pre-registered 4-seed escalation.
predictions.falsifier: The 95% CI of I(r) includes 0, or I(r) is negative, for either reader.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Nothing in the design fixes the sign of D(self)-D(foreign): both readers, both self pools and both foreign pools are actually run, so a null or reversed interaction is a directly measurable outcome and the 'CI includes 0' falsifier is easy to reach at the stated power.

predictions.depends_on: Compressor-identity ablation cells: the foreign pool (and E) re-compressed by the reader vs by the writer at L1 and L2, same reader, same retrieval.
predictions.falsifier: Reader-compressed exceeds writer-compressed by >= 4 net with CI excluding 0.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: This is an equivalence claim with a 4-point bound tested against a ~+-6 contrast half-width, so any failure to detect confirms it, and the falsifier is one-sided: a reader-compressed version 4+ points WORSE also contradicts 'changes by less than 4' without falsifying.
predictions.fix: Two-sided TOST at +-4 with seeds giving a contrast half-width <= 2, and count a large negative difference as falsifying too.

predictions.depends_on: L2 cells for each writer versus the Measurement C static six-procedure prompt per reader; all gains are already reported net of that prompt, so this contrast is the L2 net gain itself.
predictions.falsifier: X-written or Q-written procedures beat the static prompt by >= 4 net with CI excluding 0.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Another 4-point bound against ~+-6 noise, stated as a universal null over several L2 cells, so non-detection confirms it and only an implausibly large single-cell effect could falsify.
predictions.fix: Recast as an equivalence test with a pre-registered bound and power (half-width <= 2), or pre-register that any single L2 cell whose CI lies above 0 falsifies.

predictions.depends_on: Foreign L0 and L2 gains divided by the same reader's self-pool gains at the same level - i.e. exactly the four cell means that already produce P1, P2 and P3; no CI or noise figure is stated for the ratio.
predictions.falsifier: ratio(L2) <= ratio(L0) for some foreign writer x reader pair.
predictions.label: entailed
predictions.reason: If P1 holds (g_self(L0) > g_self(L2)) and P2 holds (g_for(L2) > g_for(L0)), then ratio(L2)=g_for(L2)/g_self(L2) exceeds ratio(L0) by arithmetic on shared measured terms, so the falsifier is just the negation of P1/P2 and P6 tests nothing new.
predictions.fix: Replace with an estimand not built from the same four means (e.g. absolute foreign gain against an independent expert or third-writer denominator) reported with its own bootstrap CI and a margin larger than that CI.

shared_terms: P1-P3: D(self) is one term of I(r)=D(self)-D(foreign); the same self-L0 and self-L2 means determine both.
P2-P3: D(foreign) is the other term of I(r), so P3 is fixed once P1 and P2 are measured on the same four cells.
P1-P2-P6: ratio(L)=g_foreign(L)/g_self(L) is a ratio of those same four cell means, so P6 is an arithmetic consequence of P1 and P2.
P4-P5: both are scored on the foreign L2 gain net of the static prompt, so a single cell mean moves both.
compression_erases_the_writer.headline: P3

own_errors_pass_the_gate.name: own_errors_pass_the_gate

predictions.depends_on: C1 (procedure graft) at 50% bank rate vs the clean bank in the Q->Qwen3 downstream cell, 674 games x 2 seeds, half-width ~+-5 net, with a 100% cell as an existence check.
predictions.falsifier: Harm < 6 net at 50% and also at 100%.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: A reader that ignores or repairs grafted wrong procedures (1.5 expected contaminated items among k=3) simply shows no success loss, and the 100% backstop roughly doubles the effect, so the no-harm world is separable from the >=6 world at the stated half-width.

predictions.depends_on: 2x2 D0 verification cells {Qwen3, EXAONE} x {Q hosts, X hosts} on C1 items, >=600 planted and >=600 clean per cell, recall SE ~2 and interaction SE ~4, with the headline family pre-selected so foreign-host recall lies in 30-80%.
predictions.falsifier: recall(self host) >= recall(foreign host) for either reader, or both readers showing the same host ordering (pool-difficulty main effect, no interaction).
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Both readers are crossed with both host pools on identically edited, game-paired items and the ceiling/floor rule keeps recall off the rails, so a null, a reversal, or a pure pool main effect are all measurable against the 10-point margin at a 4-point interaction SE.

predictions.depends_on: Paraphrase arm: foreign contaminated items rewritten by the reader with the planted error script-verified to survive, re-verified by D0, with per-item reader NLL logged.
predictions.falsifier: Recall within +-4 of the unparaphrased original ALTHOUGH NLL falls by the amount seen for self hosts.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The falsifier is gated on the paraphrase actually driving NLL down to self-host levels - an outcome the design neither guarantees, measures against a tolerance, nor controls - and the +-4 equivalence band is inside the ~+-5.6 half-width of a recall difference at SE ~2 per arm.
predictions.fix: Pre-register an NLL-matching criterion (retain only paraphrases within a stated NLL distance of self-host items and report the qualifying fraction) plus a two-sided equivalence bound with item counts giving half-width <= 3.

predictions.depends_on: D1 (static six-procedure prompt inside the verification context) vs D0 recall on self hosts and on foreign hosts, per reader, on the same planted item sets.
predictions.falsifier: D1 self-host recall within +-4 of D0.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: Only the first clause carries a falsifier: the gap-halving clause the hypothesis rests on can fail (D1 lifting foreign-host recall equally, leaving the gap intact) with no stated falsifying outcome, and the +-4 band is inside the recall-difference noise.
predictions.fix: Add an explicit falsifier on the gap estimand (gap_D1 > 0.5 x gap_D0 with CI excluding), score D0 and D1 on identical paired items, and size the cells for a half-width <= 3.

predictions.depends_on: 30% C1 cells for Q hosts and X hosts with the Qwen3 reader and their clean-bank denominators; each gain carries half-width ~+-5 net, and clean foreign gain is expected to be smaller than clean self gain.
predictions.falsifier: leverage(foreign) >= leverage(self) with CI excluding the 0.15 margin.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Leverage is a ratio whose denominator is itself a +-5 gain that differs between self and foreign pools, so the CI on the 0.15 difference is far wider than the margin (and the normalisation actually pushes against the prediction whenever the foreign clean gain is the smaller denominator).
predictions.fix: Score absolute harm (clean minus contaminated net points) per host with a paired cluster bootstrap and a margin at least twice the reported half-width, or add seeds until the leverage CI is under 0.15.

predictions.depends_on: Rate-0 three-writer clean store per reader with no gate, D0 gate, D1 gate and writer-identity gate; FPR measured on >=600 clean foreign items (SE ~1.6 points), cost measured in net points at +-5 per cell.
predictions.falsifier: D0 gate false-positive rate on clean foreign items >= 20%, or its cost >= 6 net.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The second clause is true by construction - the writer-identity gate deletes every foreign item, so its cost IS the mixed-store minus self-store gain, the same quantity it is compared with - and the <3 vs >=6 cost band lies inside the +-5 per-cell noise, leaving only the FPR clause genuinely able to fail.
predictions.fix: Drop or restate the identity-gate clause as a measured quantity with its own CI, and set the cost falsifier at a margin at least twice the +-5 half-width (or add seeds on the gated cells).

shared_terms: P2-P3: the unparaphrased foreign-host D0 recall is the same measurement in both, so P3's baseline is P2's foreign-host cell.
P2-P4: P4's self-foreign recall gap IS P2's estimand, so a null in P2 leaves P4's halving clause undefined.
P1-P5: P5's leverage numerator and denominator are built from the same clean-bank and C1-contaminated Q->Qwen3 cells that produce P1's Gate-0 harm.
P5-P6: both rest on the clean self vs clean foreign gains (P6's 'foreign excess over the self pool', P5's clean denominators).

search_disposition_contagion.name: search_disposition_contagion

predictions.depends_on: P8 padded pool vs W1 at k=3 for the Qwen3 reader, 674 games x 2 seeds, half-width ~+-5 net; padded sequences replayed in the environment to confirm they still succeed.
predictions.falsifier: Harm < 6 net at dose 8.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: A reader that ignores 8 inserted useless search actions simply shows no success loss and that null is measurable at the stated half-width; the padding does inflate injected tokens at fixed k=3, which confounds the interpretation of any harm but does not close off the falsifying outcome.

predictions.depends_on: Reader mean search length (measured from environment observations, receptacle visits before the target is first observed) regressed on pool mean search length across W1, W2, W3, P2, P4, P8, with game-level pairing and cluster bootstrap; SE ~0.2 steps per cell.
predictions.falsifier: The 95% CI of beta includes 0, i.e. the reader's search is invariant to the retrieved search.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: The six pools span a wide, independently manipulated x-range (including a padding dose ladder whose search length is set by construction) while the outcome is a separate environment-side measurement, so beta=0 is fully reachable and a 0.3 slope is well outside the 0.2-step cell noise.

predictions.depends_on: Disposition-matched subsample cells (W4 and W5 subsampled to W2's search-length distribution) compared with the W2 cell, reader search length at SE ~0.2 per cell.
predictions.falsifier: A matched foreign pool yields a reader search length differing from W2's by >= 2 steps with CI excluding 0.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: A 2-step identity effect is roughly six times the ~0.3-step SE of the difference and both foreign backbones are run matched against a same-backbone variant, so the falsifier is reachable and separable, although the 1-2 step band decides nothing and the matched subsample assumes untested overlap between the foreign and W2 search-length distributions.

predictions.depends_on: Manipulation-only segment cells (task line + trajectory from the first take onward) for W3 and P8, retained-gain ratio against W1's full-item gain, plus reader search length against the k=0 level.
predictions.falsifier: Manipulation-only loses >= half the gain (stated as produced by the W1 manipulation-only vs full cells) or search length stays >= 2 steps above k=0 (W3 manipulation-only cell).
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The gain falsifier is scored on the W1 cells while the claim is about W3 and P8 manipulation-only items, the 0.5-0.75 retention band is inside the ratio's CI (a +-5 to +-7 numerator over a ~+27 denominator), and the search clause is one-sided so a manipulation-only segment that pushes search BELOW k=0 - which it can, since the first take names the receptacle holding the target - contradicts 'within 1 step' without falsifying.
predictions.fix: State the retention falsifier on the W3 and P8 manipulation-only cells themselves, make the search-length claim a two-sided band around k=0, and report the retained-gain ratio CI so that 0.75 vs 0.5 lies outside it.

predictions.depends_on: Full-item cells, Kendall tau between the reader's visit order and the retrieved item's order over shared receptacles, against a rank-10 same-type same-room-class item the reader never saw.
predictions.falsifier: The CI of the tau difference includes 0.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: The placebo is a lower-ranked item, so the injected item is by retrieval selection more similar to the current game than the placebo is; the reader's own layout-driven visit order therefore produces a positive tau difference with no copying at all, making the falsifier reachable only if that selection artifact happens to be absent - a mechanism the design neither names nor controls.
predictions.fix: Use the SAME top-ranked retrieved item as the placebo, scored on episodes where it was never injected (k=0 or search-stripped arms), or match the placebo to the injected item on retrieval score and receptacle overlap.

predictions.depends_on: Read-time ranking check (G8) at dose 4: the reader ranks its k=3 retrieved items by expected usefulness and recall of placing padded items last is scored per dose - but a Pd cell's bank is entirely padded W1 items, and no mixed bank is specified.
predictions.falsifier: Recall >= 0.7 at dose 4 with CI excluding 0.5.
predictions.label: entailed
predictions.reason: When every retrieved item is padded, at most one of the three padded items can occupy the last position, so recall is capped near 1/3 and the >=0.7 falsifier is arithmetically unreachable; the retriever cannot deliver the unpadded contrast items the prediction is about.
predictions.fix: Run the read-time check on a mixed bank (padded and unpadded items at a stated rate within the retrieved type), or as a forced choice between the padded and unpadded version of the same trajectory, with the chance level stated.

shared_terms: P1-P2: both are produced by the same P8-vs-W1 full-item episodes (P1's success loss and the high-dose endpoint that dominates the slope).
P2-P3: P3 conditions on the very pool-mean-search-length regressor that defines P2's slope, so a beta near 0 makes P3's '<1 step' claim automatic.
P2-P4: P4's 'search length within 1 step of k=0' is the same reader-search-length outcome as P2, measured on the segment-stripped version of the same W3/P8 pools.
P1-P4: P4's retained-gain ratio uses W1's full-item gain as its denominator, the same cell that anchors P1's harm contrast.
